questions.q: What does a dataset security predicate do?
options: It filters which rows a user can retrieve from the dataset at query time
It decides which dashboards exist in an app
It encrypts the dataset file
It schedules dataset refreshes
questions.explain: A predicate is a filter condition applied per user; non-matching rows are simply not returned.

questions.q: A dataset has no security predicate and a rep can open the app. What can the rep see?
options: Only their own records automatically
Nothing
Every row of the dataset
Only records from their role
questions.explain: Without a predicate, anyone who can query the dataset can see all of its rows.

options: Show every row to every user
Hide all rows
Match rows by dataset name
Return a row only if its OwnerId column equals the logged-in user's Id
questions.explain: It's an ownership predicate: a row passes only when the owner matches the current user.

questions.q: Which practice is recommended when validating a predicate?
options: Test only as a system administrator
Test as ordinary users, including one who owns records and one who owns none
Skip testing if the syntax looks right
Test only after the dashboard is shared org-wide
questions.explain: Admin sessions can hide problems, so test with realistic non-admin users covering multiple cases.

questions.q: Rows from a warehouse table are joined into a dataset. What is needed before a predicate can restrict them by user?
options: Nothing, Salesforce sharing rules apply automatically
A longer app name
A larger API allowance
A column in the dataset that maps each row to a user or team
questions.explain: Predicates compare dataset columns to user attributes, so external rows need a mapping column first.
